Markus,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team found the latency and end-to-end throughput promising. Procurement asked us to get a tighter readout on unit economics before we can move to SOW and budget signoff. Can you send a short spreadsheet or readout we can attach to the MAP? Ideally we need this by next Tuesday so our procurement committee can include it in the formal MAP milestone list.

Best,

Hi Lydia — great to hear the demo landed well.

I attached a draft MAP workbook (MAP_draft_v3.xlsx) with a tokens-per-dollar model and a short sensitivity table tied to three configurations: hosted (standard), hosted + prefix KV cache, and dedicated with 4x batching. Key takeaways up front:
- Baseline tokens/$ (hosted, no cache, per your traffic): ~0.0028 USD/token generated (model: rw-large-v2 quantized)
- With prefix KV cache for repeated prompts (assume 30% cache-hit on generation path) effective tokens/$ drops to ~0.0020
- Aggressive batching (4–8 reqs per batch) reduces infra cost but increases 95th p latency by ~60–120 ms; we included a small sim.

Requested timeline: I can get the completed workbook and a short one-pager by Mon 9/20 for your procurement packet. If procurement needs faster, we can ship a one-page summary today and follow with the workbook.

Quick ask to my team (Ben / Rishi): can you verify the latency at 95th p for the 4x batching path (attached sim CSV) and confirm assumptions on tokenization overhead? I annotated the assumptions tab in the draft.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Markus — attaching the sim CSV (batching_sim_results.csv) and a short note. Highlights:
- 4x batching gives ~27% reduction in GPU token compute cost vs 1x, 8x batching ~38%.
- 95th p latency impact observed in the sim (hosted infra): +95ms at 4x, +220ms at 8x (these numbers include network tail and queuing under pilot traffic spikes).
- Tokenization overhead: ~2–4% on average for medium prompts; for long prompts (1k+ tokens) overhead reaches ~7–9% due to multi-chunking and tokenizer passes.

I updated the MAP_draft_v3.xlsx assumptions tab and included a small sensitivity worksheet. Also attached tokens_per_dollar_model.pdf as a compact explainer.

If procurement needs a gating rule, suggest: "Acceptance contingent on observed avg cache-hit >= 25% during pilot week AND 95th p latency for production route <= 800ms with 4x batching." We can make that stricter for Dedicated.

-Ben
